method: Read each complete answer in isolation against the frozen established scope and first twenty entries of expanded-v5/grading-scope.json. No fact borrowed from another question, reader, or summary to complete the answer. Summary/source evidence establishes correctness and support, not omitted answer content. Confidence and support labels are not grades.

cases.answer: The adviser limit is up to 3 total cards, counting faceup and facedown. Before exceeding the limit, discard an adviser (respecting locked cards); if the incoming card changes the limit, use the new limit before playing it, and use the lowest limit if there are multiple limit-changing cards. A facedown adviser has no suit, restriction banner, or power; later it can be played faceup to a legal destination or discarded as a minor action, and it may be peeked at. A faceup adviser cannot be discarded at will, only when another rule permits or requires it. An Exile may reveal a true Vision faceup in the separate Revealed Vision space, which does not use an adviser slot; doing so replaces and discards the Exile’s previous revealed Vision. Chancellor/Citizens may hold true Visions facedown but cannot reveal them.

cases.answer: Search either the world deck or the discard pile for the pawn's region, never both. A discard-pile Search costs 2 Supply. World-deck Search costs 2 when zero Visions have been drawn, 3 at 1–2, and 4 at 3–5; Darkest Secret replaces that world-deck cost with 2, with other modifiers still applying. Draw up to 3, one at a time from the world deck; a world-deck Vision must be announced, immediately stops the draw, and advances Visions Drawn by 1. A Vision drawn from a discard pile neither stops drawing nor advances the track.
cases.borderline_issue: Whether Draw up to 3 alone conveys the prescribed three-card draw and constrained reasons for drawing fewer.
decisive_answer_quotes: Draw up to 3, one at a time from the world deck; a world-deck Vision must be announced, immediately stops the draw, and advances Visions Drawn by 1.
